title: TATAR findings-only feed
description: Shared findings.json contract emitted by every TATAR collector alongside summary.json: the findings-only feed for SOAR / SIEM ingestion. The findings[] definition is kept byte-identical to summary.schema.json#/properties/findings (asserted by tests/run-tests.sh) so this file validates standalone, with no $ref resolver.

tool.description: Human tool name, e.g. 'TATAR Triage Toolkit'. Identical across platforms; 'platform' is the discriminator.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS shared schema. Consumers key off this. 1.3 only ADDS optional finding properties, so a 1.2 consumer keeps working against a 1.3 document.

generated.description: ISO-8601 time the feed was written (the run's finish time).

findingsCount.description: Length of findings[]; equals activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount.

activeFindingsCount.description: Findings still on the headline list. INVARIANT: activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount == findings.length. A low value means 'allowlisted' only when suppressedCount is high - it never means the host is clean.

suppressedCount.description: Findings hidden by an allowlist rule but retained in findings[] for audit. INVARIANT: activeFindingsCount + suppressedCount == findings.length.

findings.description: Automated triage leads (NOT verdicts). Each maps to zero or more MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

severity.description: The shipped collectors emit only High and Review. Info is reserved for low-signal context findings; a consumer may receive it from a future collector, so handle it, but do not expect it today.

category.description: Emitting module/collector, e.g. process, users, persistence.

technique.description: Suggested MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs. Empty when unmapped.

detail.description: Where to look / why it matters.

confidence.description: How sure the tool is (independent of severity).

suppressed.description: True when hidden from the headline by an allowlist rule (still retained for audit).

suppressReason.description: Why the finding was suppressed (allowlist rule / signature).

iocMatch.description: True when an IOC matched this finding. Since 1.3 the indicator itself is in iocIndicator; it is still prefixed into detail as 'IOC match: <indicator> | ...' for human readers.

confidenceReason.description: Why the tool assigned this confidence, in plain words. Derived from the same rule that derives confidence, so the number is auditable without having to read the collector. Added in 1.3; empty when unknown.

iocIndicator.description: The indicator from the supplied IOC feed that matched, when iocMatch is true; empty otherwise. Before 1.3 this could only be read by parsing the 'IOC match: <indicator> | ...' prefix of detail, which is still written for human readers.

module.description: The collector module that raised this finding, e.g. process, persistence. Added in 1.3; the IOC evidence pass uses 'ioc'.

collected_at.description: UTC time the finding was raised, ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Earlier than 'generated' by however long the remaining modules took. Added in 1.3.

paths.description: Absolute paths this finding names, de-duplicated, in order of appearance. This is exactly the set the allowlist, publisher, hash and IOC passes can reach, so it is also the audit trail for a suppression decision: a finding with an empty paths[] can never be suppressed by a path, publisher or hash rule. Added in 1.3.

then.description: From schemaVersion 1.4 every timestamp in this document is ISO 8601 UTC at second precision - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ - on every platform. Earlier versions are not held to it: the Windows producer wrote local time with an offset while the Linux producer wrote Z, so output from the two editions could not be sorted together and a 1.3 document carried both shapes at once (collected_at in Z beside generated with an offset). Constrained here rather than only described, because 'ISO-8601 string' was what the 1.1 schema already said.
